# The Glow That Follows the Turning

## Scripture
"As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease." — Genesis 8:22

## Reflection

Autumn ushers in a peculiar shift in the night sky. The Summer Triangle begins its slow descent toward the western horizon, while the Great Square of Pegasus rises in the east—a celestial marker that the seasons are turning, exactly as they have since the days of Noah.

Yet there is a subtle wonder here that we often miss. Even as one constellation surrenders to another, the sky never goes dark. The stars we lose in the west are replaced by new ones in the east. And always, the steady glow of the Milky Way arcs overhead, a reminder that the turning of seasons is not chaos—it is rhythm.

God’s promise to Noah wasn’t merely about the rainbow. It was about the enduring reliability of creation. The same God who sets Pegasus in motion also sets the harvest into your hands and the quiet into your evenings. The changes you face—the endings that feel like loss—are not signs that God has abandoned you. They are evidence that He keeps His word.

When the constellations turn, they turn faithfully. When your seasons shift, you are held by the same faithful hand. You can trust the turning, because you can trust the One who turns it.

## Prayer
Faithful Creator, when my seasons change and the familiar fades, help me see Your steady hand in every turning. You have never failed to keep Your promises, and You will not fail now. Amen.
